The load priority can be splitted into two sections, one with ﬁxed priority which cannot be changed during runtime and one with variable priority. Parameter deﬁnes the number of loads with ﬁxed priority. Fixed priority range always starts with static priority 1 (highest sta- tic priority) and ends with value of parameter. A ﬁxed priority can never be overwritten by an dynamic priority. Thus, a ﬁxed priority is always higher than a variable one. Example for value 2: Loads sorted by static priority: [5 2 | 1 4 3] load 5 will always have priority 1, load 2 priority 2. Priority 3 and higher can be assigned to loads 1, 4 and 3 and vary due to dynamic priority.
X axis stands for the vehicle coordinator state, Y axis for the static priority. The values stand for the load number (numbering according to assignment in FC Eem_EgyMngtAdpr).

Factor for power derating of load in dependency of utilization of electrical system and load. Values between 0 and 1, where 1 means 0% and 0 means 100% derating. For certain loads, matching of desired operation point and actual operation point can be determined based on the power demand (e.g. when cabin temperature is close to setpoint, air conditioner will request less power than when far from setpoint). So, derating of the climate compressor power might be possible without knowledge of driver.

When system is operating at 100% of the available power, it might lead to violating the bat- tery limits in case that a component connected to the electrical system consumes more power than expected (e.g. 1010W instead of 1000W). Parameter gives the possibility to ap- ply a power buffer to ensure, that system is not operated at 100% of available power.
